ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates under FICA. All directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories must be screened against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, the United Kingdom Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list, the Australian DFAT consolidated list, and the Financial Intelligence Centre's domestic targeted financial sanctions list. Screening must include adverse media, global watchlists, FATF-publicized jurisdictions, and transactional red flags; screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Portal — https://eservices.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A private company name must use Latin (Roman) alphabet characters; non-Roman scripts and ideograms are not accepted. The name may be drawn from any of the Republic's official languages, provided it is transliterated into Roman script. Names must include the suffix '(Pty) Ltd' for a private company and may not contain misleading, offensive, nepotistic, or state-implying expressions. Acceptable punctuation is generally limited to spaces, full stops, commas, ampersands, apostrophes and hyphens.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving a notice of refusal from the CIPC, an applicant may either file a fresh name reservation or institute an administrative appeal under section 13(2) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 by submitting a notice of appeal to the CIPC within 15 business days of the refusal notice. The appeal is adjudicated by the Companies Tribunal, which may set aside or confirm the CIPC decision. In respect of a restricted name, the applicant may alternatively apply to the Minister for condonation in terms of section 15(3) after securing the relevant regulatory approval or a letter of no objection. During the pendency of the appeal or condonation application, the applicant should not incur contractual obligations relying on the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. A virtual office or bundled-registered-office service is acceptable only if the service provider maintains a physical street address in South Africa, receives legal and regulatory process, stores the company's statutory records, and allows regulators access during business hours. P.O. Box addresses and pure digital mailboxes are impermissible. For a used heavy machinery trading company in the ISIC 4659 sector, SARS, customs authorities and commercial lenders will ordinarily expect additional physical trading premises, a contracted warehouse, or a bonded inspection yard to substantiate commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to elevated — estimated 20–30% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by SARS Customs and Excise, the Income Tax branch, the Financial Intelligence Centre, or municipal business-licensing inspectors, driven by the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier and the high-value, moveable, construction-asset nature of the business.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 8(2)(b), 11-16, 19, 23, 66-69 read with Companies Regulations 2011, Regs 7-10; prescribed forms CoR 9.1, CoR 14.1, CoR 14.2/14.2A and CoR 14.3.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) accompanied by the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.2 / amended CoR 14.2A)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private company; the Companies Act 71 of 2008 abolished par-value shares and authorised capital. No escrow deposit is required. The initial share consideration is fixed by the directors in the MOI (commonly R1.00 per ordinary share) and must be paid in cash prior to the issue of share certificates.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION of [Company Name] (Pty) Ltd (Reg. No. [complete]). (1) RESOLVED that the incorporation of the company and the adoption of the Memorandum of Incorporation be and are hereby ratified and confirmed. (2) RESOLVED that the subscription for [number] ordinary shares at R[amount] per share, fully paid in cash, by the initial subscribers be approved and that share certificates be issued accordingly. (3) RESOLVED that the registered office be and is hereby fixed at [full physical address, city, province], South Africa. (4) RESOLVED that [names] be appointed as first directors, with [name] appointed as Managing Director vested with day-to-day authority. (5) RESOLVED that the directors be authorised to open bank accounts and finalise all SARS and statutory registrations. Passed unanimously this [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Company Name with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) - e-Services online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the CIPC e-Services portal using a registered user account or a mandated XBRL-accredited issuing agent. Submit Form CoR 9.1 to reserve the proposed name, selecting the suffix '(Pty) Ltd'. Pay the statutory name reservation fee (currently ZAR 50) electronically in the portal. The CIPC examiner checks the name against section 11 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for availability and undesirability, then issues a Name Reservation Certificate valid for six months (extendable by two months).
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form CoR 9.1 Name Reservation Application
Certified identity copies of all incorporators
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the CIPC will cite the statutory grounds; file an objection or re-application using a revised CoR 9.1 with alternative name proposals, or apply to the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for an adjudication of disputed names within 20 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare the Memorandum of Incorporation and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating attorneys / directors (drafting only; no filing window at this stage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation using the standard template (Form CoR 14.2) or an amended MOI (Form CoR 14.2A) under sections 15-16 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. For a private company, include the mandatory restrictions under section 8(2)(b): prohibition on offering shares to the public, a 50-shareholder cap, and share transfer restrictions. Record the registered office address, first directors, and capital structure without par value. Each proposed director must sign a formal consent and eligibility declaration under section 69 of the Act for annexure to the Notice of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Signed consent to act as director from each director (section 66)
Certified identity copies of all directors and incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the draft is not compliant, legal counsel must amend the restrictions to align with section 8(2)(b) of the Act; re-execute the MOI and director consents before submission. Any amendment post-incorporation will require a subsequent special resolution filed under section 16.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Notice of Incorporation and MOI with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) - e-Filing / electronic submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) electronically, attaching the MOI, the name reservation number, and the directors' consents and declarations. Pay the company registration fee (currently ZAR 175) plus applicable supplementary fees in the CIPC portal. CIPC verifies compliance with sections 13-14 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and Companies Regulations 7-10. Upon acceptance, CIPC allocates a unique enterprise registration number; no notarisation is required for standard filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a notice of defective filing, correct the specific deficiency and resubmit through e-Filing within 10 business days as per Regulation 9(3) of the Companies Regulations 2011. If the application is rejected on the merits, file a fresh application with corrected documentation or approach the Companies Tribunal for review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Convene First Board Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC (certificate issuance) / Board of Directors (internal statutory formalities)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once CIPC approves the filing, it issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3) as prima facie evidence of registration. Immediately thereafter convene the First Board Meeting, adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution (covering share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments), issue share certificates, and open the statutory records required by sections 24-27 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, including the securities register, director register, and registered office record.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the First Board Meeting signed by the chairperson
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not received within the SLA, escalate via the CIPC contact centre and request a status verification; if the certificate contains clerical errors, file a rectification application under section 81 of the Companies Act; if lost, apply for a duplicate certificate upon payment of the prescribed CIPC fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with SARS and Local Municipality for Business Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) and Local Municipality (Business Act 71 of 1991)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly incorporated company with SARS for income tax, and for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) if employees are hired, within 21 business days after incorporation through eFiling; a corporate income tax number and Tax Compliance Status (TCS) are issued. Compulsory VAT registration applies when taxable supplies exceed or reasonably will exceed ZAR 1 million in any 12-month period. Apply for municipal zoning and business licence under the Business Act 71 of 1991; a warehouse or trade yard is ordinarily exempt but local by-laws may require registration. Register with the Compensation Fund under COIDA through the Department of Employment and Labour.
required_dossiers: Directors' identity documents and bank account details
Lease agreement or title deed for the business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the registration, respond to the eFiling request within 10 business days to avoid administrative penalties (ZAR 250 to ZAR 16,000); if the municipality refuses the licence, appeal to the Municipal Planning Tribunal for a use-rights departure or submit a revised zoning application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic) together with the International Trade Administration Commission (ITAC), National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS), and the South African Police Service (SAPS) for Second-Hand Goods Dealer registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: SAPS Second-Hand Goods Dealer Registration Certificate (Second-Hand Goods Act 6 of 2009); NRCS Letter of Authority for Import of Used Plant and Machinery (if cross-border imports occur); ITAC Import Permit under the International Trade Administration Act 71 of 2002

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) / Provincial Environmental Authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a compulsory full Environmental Impact Assessment for ordinary wholesale warehousing and trade yards under the EIA Regulations 2014 (Listing Notices 1-3); a Basic Assessment may be triggered only where significant site development, bulk infrastructure or activity in a sensitive environment is undertaken. An environmental registration may be required by provincial bylaws for storage of hazardous fluids.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial discharge is generated by wholesale trading; where wash bays exist, effluent must comply with municipal trade-effluent bylaws under the Water Services Act 108 of 1997 (typical parameters: pH 5.5-9.5, TSS not exceeding 500 mg/L, COD not exceeding 1,000 mg/L). Used oils, coolants and batteries are hazardous wastes under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008; storage must meet SANS 10234 classification and SANS 0895 Part 3 requirements, with removal only by registered waste transporters. Emissions from diesel engines of traded machines, if operated, must remain below National Ambient Air Quality Standards under the Air Quality Act 39 of 2004; dust suppression measures must be applied to open yards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the local Fire Protection Services after inspection under the National Building Regulations (SANS 10400) and municipal fire bylaws; structural load assessment of racking and heavy-plant storage areas certified by a registered professional engineer; Certificate of Compliance for electrical installations issued by an accredited electrician; workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, including the appointment of health and safety officers and registration with the Compensation Fund (COIDA) through the Department of Employment and Labour.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), established under the South African Revenue Service Act 34 of 1997. Primary transactional portals: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za) for income tax and VAT registration/returns; SARS Customs & Excise module for import/export declarations and excise registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Proprietary Limited (Pty) Ltd: (i) incorporate through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) to obtain the company registration number; (ii) appoint a resident public officer as required by s. 252 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011; (iii) register for income tax on SARS eFiling, obtaining the income tax reference number (the company TIN); (iv) submit a VAT101 application to register as a VAT vendor within 21 days after taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any rolling 12-month period (voluntary registration available from ZAR 50,000); (v) obtain an importer/exporter customs code through the SARS Customs registration process (DA185) prior to physical exports; (vi) register for PAYE, SDL, and UIF when employees are engaged. Non-resident owners may hold 100% of the shares, but the South African legal entity is the registered taxpayer; no separate foreign-entity TIN is issued for a branch unless a permanent establishment of a non-resident company is registered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A resident (Pty) Ltd is taxed as a company on its worldwide income at 27% corporate income tax for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; no pass-through eligibility. Territorial scope: residence-based worldwide taxation. Tax-exempt zones: no general tax holiday applies; special economic zone (SEZ) concessions (e.g., reduced CIT and s. 12I allowance) are limited to SEZ-designated qualifying operators, not to general wholesale traders of used machinery.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections include: (i) VAT group registration election under s. 50 of the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991 for connected/related vendors; (ii) election to account for VAT on the payments basis under s. 15 of the VAT Act where the vendor meets qualifying turnover criteria; (iii) small business corporation tax treatment under s. 12E of the Income Tax Act if statutory ownership and turnover thresholds are satisfied; (iv) foreign tax credit election under s. 6quat of the Income Tax Act for foreign taxes suffered on export or foreign-source income; (v) hybrid mismatch rules (ss. 8F, 8FA, 23M, and 25H of the Income Tax Act) are mandatory anti-avoidance provisions, not elective, and impose deemed interest or deduction denials that must be disclosed on the ITR14 return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS; unitary national system with no sub-national sales tax overlay.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 (compulsory VAT registration when taxable supplies exceed this amount in any consecutive 12-month period); ZAR 50,000 (voluntary registration threshold). Non-resident suppliers of imported services to South African recipients may be subject to the reverse-charge mechanism under s. 7(1)(c) of the VAT Act even without local registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory tax-authority API clearance regime is currently in force. SARS accepts paper and electronic VAT invoices that satisfy s. 20 of the VAT Act (vendor name, address, VAT number, invoice description, quantity, price, tax amount, and 'tax invoice' legend). VAT returns are filed electronically via eFiling (VAT201), and customs export declarations are lodged through the SARS Customs EDI platform. SARS has published a draft national e-invoicing framework with a phased mandate expected in future years; until legislated, no authorization token or real-time clearance code is required, but all original electronic invoices must be retained in unaltered form for audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act zero-rates the supply of movable goods, including secondhand hydraulic earthmovers and rollers, where the vendor physically exports the goods (or delivers them to an export enterprise) within 90 days of the date of supply, under customs supervision, and retains documentary proof of export. The 0% rate applies to the export sale; input VAT on the purchase of used equipment is creditable under s. 16(3) of the VAT Act provided valid tax invoices are held and the goods are not deemed supplied or apportioned for mixed use. The goods must permanently leave South Africa; re-importation generally invalidates the zero-rating. Offshore services incidental to the export (e.g., international freight) are not within s. 11(1)(a) but may be considered separately under s. 11(2)(k) if the service is physically rendered and consumed outside South Africa; for this goods-trading model, s. 11(1)(a) is the operative zero-rating ground.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500 / DA 500) electronically lodged with and cleared by SARS Customs
Bill of Lading (sea freight), Air Waybill (air freight), or CMR consignment note (road freight) showing South Africa as origin and a foreign consignee/destination
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the SAD 500, with unit serial numbers, model designations, and declared customs values
SWIFT MT103 or bank inward remittance certificate (IRC) evidencing receipt of export proceeds in a South African bank account
Exchange control settlement record (EXM form / authorised dealer certification) where required by the South African Reserve Bank
Proof of physical departure (terminal gate pass, outturn report, or border customs stamp) for the relevant transport mode
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS reconciles export zero-ratings against customs SAD 500 clearances, bills of lading, freight-forwarder files, and bank settlement records. If goods are not exported within 90 days of supply, the transaction is re-characterised as standard-rated at 15%, triggering retrospective output VAT, interest, and penalties under the VAT Act. Invalid or missing export evidence causes reversal of the zero-rating and clawback of all input VAT claimed on the equipment. Under s. 59 of the VAT Act, additional tax may be imposed at rates from 10% to 200% of the shortfall depending on conduct. Understatement penalties under s. 222 of the Tax Administration Act range from 25% to 200% of the tax shortfall for undisclosed or incorrect positions. Fraudulent zero-rating is a serious tax crime under s. 234 of the Tax Administration Act, carrying a fine of up to ZAR 7,500,000 and/or imprisonment of up to 10 years. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days additionally breaches South African Reserve Bank exchange control rules, exposing the exporter to financial penalties and potential suspension of customs trading privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) is the statutory exchange-control authority under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933, supported by the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual (CEM). Banking supervision is performed by the SARB Prudential Authority under the Banks Act 94 of 1990. All cross-border foreign-exchange transactions must be executed through a SARB-licensed Authorised Dealer in Foreign Exchange (AD), being the tier-1 commercial banks and their registered branches.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa is an IMF Article VIII member: current-account flows (trade settlement, service fees, royalties, dividends) are fully convertible without prior SARB approval and with no quantitative limit. The rand (ZAR) is a fully deliverable onshore currency. Capital-account flows are partially liberalised: inbound foreign direct investment (FDI) requires no prior exchange-control approval, only ex-post declaration to FinSurv through the receiving AD, whereas outbound investment, offshore guarantees and cross-border lending by residents remain subject to CEM thresholds and allowances. Dividend/profit remittance is unrestricted once the authorised dealer verifies the source of profit and the company files a dividend declaration; 20% dividends withholding tax applies to non-resident shareholders. Practical hurdles for a used-machinery trader are not convertibility constraints but bank de-risking of counterparties in Southern African high-risk corridors and the documentary proof of no unrepatriated export proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: CEM Section B (Exports) requires that full export proceeds be received in South Africa through an authorised dealer within 180 calendar days of the shipment date (bill of lading/air waybill date). The exporter must submit the customs SAD500 export declaration and lodge a bank-copy export form before or at shipment. Mandatory conversion ratio is nil: the historical 80%/10% surrender obligations were abolished, so proceeds may be retained in a SARB-compliant Foreign Currency Account (FCA), converted to ZAR, or applied to approved foreign trade uses. Delays beyond 180 days, partial non-receipt, or exports to sanctioned destinations require FinSurv approval via the bank; non-repatriation is a criminal offence under the Currency and Exchanges Act. For re-exported secondhand excavators, the AD will cross-match the SAD500 with procurement invoices to mitigate trade-based under/over-invoicing.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited (Standard Bank CIB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational ZAR business current account; multi-currency Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR/GBP); capital escrow and auction bid-bond sub-account
Operational ZAR business account; FCA; trade-finance facility comprising commercial LC and import advance limits
Operational ZAR account; FCA; designated escrow account for used-asset auction deposits
Operational ZAR account; FCA; import/export guarantee and EBIT-linked clearing structures
Premium operational ZAR account; FCA; cross-border treasury overlay for high-value machinery transactions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW-MEDIUM - supplementary rail only; not a permitted primary treasury gateway. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, dLocal) do not hold SARB Authorised Dealer status and may not settle export proceeds or import payments for a South African resident without routing through a licensed AD. Channeling sale or supplier funds via an unlicensed EMI would breach the Currency and Exchanges Act and the FIC Act because cross-border transaction reports flow only through AD bank channels. A South African-licensed payment fintech (third-party payment provider under the National Payment System Act, 1998) may handle domestic ZAR collection via PASA rails, and foreign EMIs may cover incidental low-value disbursements (corporate cards, SaaS fees), but all FX conversion, trade settlement, LC issuance and escrow operations for used-machinery deals must remain inside a tier-1 authorised bank. Recommended architecture: local regulated EMI for small domestic receipts, tier-1 AD bank for every USD/EUR flow above USD 10,000.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory physical-presence requirement exists under FICA 38 of 2001; identity verification may be conducted non-face-to-face subject to enhanced due diligence. However, for a Medium-Risk-Enhanced machinery-trading entity with non-resident shareholders, Big-4 bank policy effectively requires (i) a video-recorded compliance interview with at least two mandated signatories and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), and (ii) for non-resident UBOs, either a physical branch visit or apostilled, liveness-verified identity and address documents. Remote account opening is accepted where the bank completes digital FICA verification (e.g., QR-based liveness), the UBO is reachable by video, and all corporate documents (CIPC extract, memorandum of incorporation, beneficial-ownership register, board resolution) are electronically certified and apostilled. A physical appearance becomes mandatory if the UBO holds a passport from a high-risk jurisdiction, if a PEP relationship is identified, or if the cross-border mandate requires a South African resident co-signatory to be met in person. Accounts are typically opened with temporary cross-border limits until the KYC step is satisfied.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flag: secondhand hydraulic excavators lack transparent pricing, creating high risk of over- or under-invoicing; banks flag appraised-value mismatches and opaque auction invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent pre-shipment inspection and appraisal by a SACPVP-registered professional machinery valuer; OEM serial-number and engine VIN verification from the manufacturer; auction-house provenance records (Ritchie Bros/Euro Auctions lot history); comparable-sales dataset for the same year, model and hour-meter class; original supplier invoice and bill of lading; registry encumbrance search confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and dual-use concern: sale or export of used excavators to countries appearing in extended sanctions profiles (Zimbabwe, Mozambique, DRC, Sudan, and Russia-affiliated buyers) triggers OFAC, EU, UN, UK and South African FIC screening failures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Positive-match-resistant sanctions screening results covering UBOs, corporate chain, vessels and consignees from the bank's list-screening engine; notarised end-user/end-use certificate; ITAC import/export authorisation where triggered; original SAD500; proof of physical movement (bill of lading, CMR, VGM certificate and vessel-tracking report).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: 100% non-resident ownership through an offshore trust or a Delaware/BVI intermediate holding company with no apparent South African economic substance; PEP exposure of the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate-chain ladder (CIPC extract plus each foreign layer's certificate of incumbency or registry search); redacted trust deed with settlor/beneficiary declaration by a regulated trustee; source-of-wealth file (12 months of audited financial statements and tax returns of the shareholder); FICA beneficial-ownership register filed at CIPC (CoR 30/31); board resolution evidencing local substance (leased yard, local managers, employment records).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Irregular inbound funding: capital injections arriving from third parties, cryptocurrency brokers or unrelated trade debtors instead of the named shareholder; inbound investment mis-coded as a loan to evade exchange control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement and SARB inward-FDI declaration filed through the bank (IMF BPM6 classification: Direct Investment - Equity Capital); foreign bank statements showing the named shareholder as originator and the corresponding interbank trail; remitting bank's licence and bank reference letter; board resolution confirming the capital purpose; funds held in escrow until the source-of-funds file is approved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return for a Proprietary Limited Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation of ZA_PTY_LTD
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC issues a compliance notice; failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off; directors may become personally liable for obligations incurred after deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and BO Schedule Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation must accompany the CIPC annual return; any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be lodged with CIPC within 5 business days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false declarations may result in CIPC enforcement notices, criminal liability for officers, monetary penalties, and possible deregistration in cases of repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14 / CIT Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the financial year-end, or by the later filing date specified in the SARS Notice of Assessment / Letter of Demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS may impose fixed monthly non-compliance penalties, understatement penalties, and interest on unpaid tax; director personal liability may arise for withholding-related taxes in cases of negligence or fraud

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual PAYE Reconciliation and EMP501 Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May for the employer tax year ending on the preceding 28 February, if the company is an employer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS may impose understatement penalties of up to 100% of the shortfall, interest, and criminal penalties for intentional non-compliance; responsible directors may be held personally liable for unremitted PAYE amounts

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit by a registered auditor is compulsory if the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more; or if the PIS is 100 to 349 and the annual financial statements were internally compiled; or if the company is a public/state-owned company or holds fiduciary assets. Private companies with PIS below 100 generally qualify for an independent review instead of an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS / IFRS for SMEs, adopted as South African Standards of Financial Reporting through the framework issued by the Financial Reporting Standards Council; local GAAP is not administered separately.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At least annually, the board or company secretary must reconcile the Register of Beneficial Ownership against all share transfers, members' records, and beneficial ownership declarations. The current beneficial ownership schedule must be submitted annually with the CIPC annual return, and any transfer of shares or change in ultimate beneficial control must be notified to CIPC within 5 business days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – USD 750 per year for a CIPC registered office, registered address, and corporate secretarial agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 7,500 per year for a small-to-medium Pty Ltd engaged in used construction equipment wholesale, subject to the applicable assurance service

stage_6.entry_description: Company's income tax reference number as registered with SARS (e.g. 9-digit SARS ID as per IT-registration confirmation).
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that the registration form (RA01/ITREG) is updated with the non-resident shareholding details; the public officer must be an SA resident.
